public_rationale: Contemporaneous reporting agrees that OpenAI expected losses and did not anticipate profitability until 2029. However, the accessible sources do not establish the full historical no-profit assertion on a consistent accounting basis. The combined claim remains unresolved. This is an evidence limitation, not a finding that Marcus was wrong.
limitations: The original financial reporting could not be read with the required tool.
Secondary summaries do not resolve the distinction between adjusted earnings, net income and cash flow.
Subsequent changes to OpenAI's forecasts would not establish what it expected in December 2024.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI has not yet made a profit and does not expect to before 2029.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI has yet to make a profit, and doesn’t anticipate making one before 2029.

from_speaker: OpenAI has yet to make a profit
our_interpretation: This describes OpenAI's financial history and its expectations as of December 11, 2024. It does not predict whether OpenAI will actually become profitable in 2029.
The ordinary reading of profit is company-wide earnings after expenses, rather than revenue, financing, gross margin or cash flow.
The post links its expectations statement to a press report, so the accounting basis is estimate.

Has yet describes the historical record through the post, rather than one quarter. The starting date is unspecified. Annual profitability is the working reading, but the sentence does not expressly exclude a profitable quarter.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable financial records establish no realized company-wide annual profit before the post, and contemporaneous reporting of internal projections establishes that OpenAI expected no annual profit before 2029.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish an earlier annual profit, or contemporaneous internal projections anticipate annual profitability before 2029.
